results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if the database project reference is ambiguous)] [Prerequisite]: Locate the intended project using SUPABASE_LIST_ALL_PROJECTS, then confirm metadata using SUPABASE_GET_PROJECT (avoid verifying the wrong environment).
[Optional (if table names/schemas are uncertain)] [Prerequisite]: Enumerate tables and views using SUPABASE_LIST_TABLES (reduce schema/name typos before querying).
[Optional (if columns/filters are uncertain or errors occur)] [Prerequisite]: Validate columns and types using SUPABASE_GET_TABLE_SCHEMAS (ensure predicates and join keys exist).

[Required] [Step]: Compute per-table counts using SUPABASE_RUN_READ_ONLY_QUERY (SELECT COUNT(*) per target table; optionally return a table,count list via UNION ALL; treat output as a single-row-per-table aggregate payload).

[Optional (if audits or deeper verification is needed)] [Next Step]: Extend checks using SUPABASE_RUN_READ_ONLY_QUERY (COUNT DISTINCT, NULL checks, GROUP BY distributions, orphan checks via NOT EXISTS; optionally add size/usage estimates where relevant).

[Optional (if spot-checking or reconciling row-level data is needed)] [Next Step]: Pull bounded, paginated rows using SUPABASE_SELECT_FROM_TABLE (use limit/offset; rely on diagnostics.total_count rather than page length).
[Fallback (if SUPABASE_RUN_READ_ONLY_QUERY fails or can’t express the query)] [Fallback]: Re-run equivalent SELECT aggregates using SUPABASE_BETA_RUN_SQL_QUERY and compare results for consistency.
[Optional (if multiple org contexts exist)] [Prerequisite]: Confirm the correct org context using GRIST_LIST_ORGANIZATIONS (avoid querying the wrong workspace).
[Optional (if docId unknown)] [Prerequisite]: Locate the target document using GRIST_LIST_WORKSPACES (capture docId for downstream calls).
[Optional (for access/reachability check)] [Prerequisite]: Validate the document is readable using GRIST_FETCH_DOCUMENT_METADATA.
[Required] [Step]: Enumerate authoritative table IDs using GRIST_LIST_TABLES (use these IDs in SQL FROM clauses).
[Optional (if column IDs are uncertain or joins fail)] [Prerequisite]: Verify column identifiers using GRIST_LIST_COLUMNS or GRIST_FETCH_TABLE_METADATA (align SQL to actual schema).
[Required] [Step]: Run a read-only validation query using GRIST_RUN_SQL_QUERY (start with small COUNT(*)/LIMIT checks before selecting wide or large-text fields).
[Optional (for cross-checking results)] [Next Step]: Sample a small slice of rows using GRIST_LIST_RECORDS (compare with SQL output when results seem truncated).

[Optional (if GRIST_RUN_SQL_QUERY returns SQLITE_ERROR like missing table/column)] [Fallback]: Re-inspect table/column identifiers using GRIST_LIST_TABLES and GRIST_LIST_COLUMNS or GRIST_FETCH_TABLE_METADATA, then rerun GRIST_RUN_SQL_QUERY.
known_pitfalls: [SUPABASE_RUN_READ_ONLY_QUERY] HTTP 400 with SQLSTATE 42P01/42703 usually indicates wrong schema/table or missing column; fix names/types before retrying.
[SUPABASE_RUN_READ_ONLY_QUERY] Aggregate outputs may be nested under response.data.result (often as single-row arrays) and values may be strings—normalize before comparing.
[SUPABASE_RUN_READ_ONLY_QUERY] Uses a project identifier field ref while SUPABASE_SELECT_FROM_TABLE uses project_ref; mixing them can cause request validation failures.
[SUPABASE_SELECT_FROM_TABLE] May return diagnostics.http_status_code=206 (partial content) and range metadata; use diagnostics.total_count plus pagination, not len(rows).
[SUPABASE_SELECT_FROM_TABLE] An out-of-range page can return diagnostics.http_status_code=416; treat as end-of-pagination, not a hard error.
[SUPABASE_BETA_RUN_SQL_QUERY] SELECT aggregates return in response.data.result (rows_affected isn’t meaningful for counts) and may hit HTTP 429 throttling—retry with backoff.
[GRIST_LIST_WORKSPACES] Downstream calls require a docId; avoid relying on a URL-derived identifier that may not match the API docId.
[GRIST_LIST_TABLES] SQL must use returned table IDs; display labels may differ, and large table lists can look truncated in previews.
[GRIST_RUN_SQL_QUERY] HTTP 400 with SQLITE_ERROR (e.g., missing table/column) usually indicates identifier/schema mismatch, not permissions.
[GRIST_RUN_SQL_QUERY] Results may appear under data.records[*].fields (and sometimes alternate shapes); normalize before downstream processing.
[GRIST_LIST_COLUMNS] Uses doc_id/table_id inputs (snake_case) while other tools commonly use docId/tableId; mismatched naming can cause call failures.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Pagination pattern for SUPABASE_SELECT_FROM_TABLE using offset/limit and diagnostics
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
def fetch_all_rows(project_ref, table, select, filters, order, page_size=1000, max_pages=1000):
    out=[]
    for i in range(max_pages):
        res=call_tool('SUPABASE_SELECT_FROM_TABLE',{'project_ref':project_ref,'table':table,'select':select,'filters':filters,'order':order,'limit':page_size,'offset':i*page_size})
        data=(res or {}).get('data',{})
        diag=data.get('diagnostics') or {}
        rows=data.get('rows') or []
        if diag.get('http_status_code')==416 or not rows: break
        out.extend(rows)
        if len(rows)<page_size: break
    return out
```

SUPABASE_RUN_READ_ONLY_QUERY.description: [Beta] Run a SQL query as supabase_read_only_user. Use when you need to safely execute SELECT queries without risk of modifying data. Only read operations are allowed.

ref.description: The unique reference ID of the Supabase project (used in the URL path). Must be exactly 20 lowercase letters (a-z). Can be found in Project Settings > General > Reference ID in the Supabase Dashboard, or from the dashboard URL: https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/<project-ref>. Can also be provided as 'project_ref'.

query.description: The SQL query to be executed as supabase_read_only_user. Only SELECT and other read-only operations are allowed. Write operations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, etc.) will be rejected. Can also be provided as 'sql'. IMPORTANT - Single Quote Handling: DO NOT double or escape single quotes in your SQL. The query is transmitted as a JSON string body, so standard SQL single quotes work directly. For example, write WHERE name = 'John' NOT WHERE name = ''John''.

parameters.description: Optional array of parameters for parameterized queries. Use $1, $2, etc. in the query to reference parameters.

SUPABASE_SELECT_FROM_TABLE.description: Tool to select rows from a Supabase/PostgREST table. Use for read-only queries with filtering, sorting, and pagination.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return (must be >= 1)

order.description: Ordering expression in the form `column.asc` or `column.desc`

table.description: Table or view name to select from

offset.description: Number of rows to skip before returning results (must be >= 0)

select.description: Comma-separated list of columns to return. Supports nested/related selections and JSON path selectors (e.g., address->postcode).

value.description: Value to compare the column against

items.description: Filter on a single column using a PostgREST operator.

filters.description: Optional list of filters. Each filter will be rendered as `<column>_<operator>=<value>` in the query string (e.g., id_eq=123). Can be provided as a list of FilterItem objects. Each FilterItem must have: column (string), operator (one of: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, ilike, is, in, cs, cd, sl, sr, nxl, nxr, adj, ov, fts, plfts, phfts, wfts), and value (the comparison value).

project_ref.description: Unique reference ID of the Supabase project (used in the hostname)

GRIST_RUN_SQL_QUERY.description: Tool to execute a read-only SQL SELECT query on a Grist document. Use after confirming the document ID and preparing a valid SQL SELECT statement.

examples: SELECT id, Name FROM Users WHERE age > ?
sql.description: SQL SELECT statement to execute. Must be a single read-only SELECT (no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE). Do not include trailing semicolon. WITH clauses and parameterized queries (using '?' placeholders) are supported.

args.description: Positional parameters to substitute for '?' placeholders in the SQL statement. Provide values in order matching the placeholders.

docId.description: Document ID of the Grist document to query. Obtain this via GRIST_LIST_WORKSPACES or from the document URL.

timeout.description: Maximum execution time in milliseconds. Default is 1000ms. Can only be reduced from the default, not increased.

GRIST_LIST_TABLES.description: Tool to list all tables within a specified document. Use after obtaining the document ID to retrieve its tables.

docId.description: The unique identifier of the Grist document to list tables from. Obtain this from GRIST_LIST_WORKSPACES or GRIST_CREATE_DOCUMENT.

SUPABASE_LIST_TABLES.description: Lists all tables and views in specified database schemas, providing a quick overview of database structure to help identify available tables before fetching detailed schemas.

schemas.description: List of schemas to search for tables (maximum 10). If not provided, lists tables from all non-system schemas. Specify schema names to limit the search to specific schemas.

project_ref.description: The unique reference ID of the Supabase project. Must be exactly 20 lowercase letters (a-z only, no numbers or hyphens). This is visible in your Supabase project URL (e.g., https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/{project_ref}).

include_views.description: Whether to include views along with tables in the results

include_metadata.description: Whether to include basic metadata like estimated row count and table size

include_system_schemas.description: Whether to include system schemas (pg_catalog, information_schema, etc.) when listing all schemas. When set to false, temporary and internal schemas such as pg_temp_*, pg_toast_temp_* and pgbouncer are excluded from the results.
